challenge.better_approach: Looked: a fixture copied from the Dell's berths would carry constrain_refs to the Dell's ~/.cairn, so off that box it is refused for an unreadable upstream, which passes the tooth for the wrong reason. A scratch chain built by the real writers is the smallest fixture that cannot do that.
challenge.hidden_assumption: That write_packet/write_constrain accept a minimal claimless packet into a tmp instance_dir; to be measured at build.
challenge.prior_art: c8e421aac06e (measured fixture for a berth only the charting box holds); MovedWorld in this same proof already patches the world for halves a and b.
challenge.real_collision: None: survey.py is not edited; the live corpus is still measured where it exists.

answers.falsifier: the proof goes green on akienasus, which holds no ~/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets, and its corpus tooth still reds if the deposit tolerance is removed
answers.how: Replace the hard-coded /home/akien/.cairn constrain berth with a scratch orient->constrain chain written in the proof's tmp; the corpus tooth adds a fixture corpus (one survey berthed through write_survey over that chain, holding MOVES_FROM, judged under MovedWorld with a forwarding order) to the live glob, and requires the fixture to be rescued.
answers.traces_to: Law 8 (a proof must read the same on every box) and Law 5 (berths are instance-space, so a proof in class-space cannot assume one).
answers.what: test_deposit_survives_a_move.py reads a berth chain it builds itself, and its corpus tooth measures a fixture corpus plus whatever corpus this box holds, so it reads the same on a box that never charted.

bullets.text: measured: ls ~/.cairn/devices/chart/0/packets on akienasus: no such directory
the corpus tooth's 'measured nothing' assert stays; the fixture is what keeps it from being vacuous on a box that never charted
